description:
Bug found while reviewing src/fetcher/crest_http_client.cr:

  - ensure_dns_cleanup_registered sets @@dns_cleanup_registered = true once
    and never resets. There is no symmetric clear/teardown method.
  - The registered Proc captures { dns_cleanup_proc.call }, which is
    itself a Proc wrapping { clear_expired_dns }. PeriodicCleanup holds
    the outer Proc forever, so calling clear_dns_cache or
    @@dns_cache_registered = false does not remove the registration.
  - Consequence: even if a future caller disables cache_enabled at
    runtime, the periodic cleanup fiber still runs clear_expired_dns on
    schedule, which still holds the @@dns_cache_lock. This is fine for
    correctness but wasteful.

Repro:

  1. Call Fetcher::CrestHttpClient.get('http://example.com/') once (this
     populates the cache and registers cleanup).
  2. Construct a second client with dns: DnsConfig.new(cache_enabled: false).
  3. Fetcher::PeriodicCleanup's registered cleanups still includes the
     DNS proc.

Fix options:

  A. Add a Fetcher::CrestHttpClient.unregister_dns_cleanup class method
     and have DnsCache expose a teardown hook.
  B. Add an at_exit hook that unregisters automatically.
  C. Refactor: the DNS cache (per the extract ticket) should own its
     lifecycle and call PeriodicCleanup.register_cleanup/unregister_cleanup
     symmetrically.

Recommend C, in coordination with the DnsCache extraction ticket. If the
extraction is deferred, ship A as a follow-up.

Test:

  spec/dns_cache_spec.cr should gain an assertion that after
  clear_dns_cache + a teardown call, PeriodicCleanup.registered_cleanups
  no longer includes the DNS proc. Use the unregister introspection
  added in #fetcherc-tbk child #1.
title: Fix DNS cache cleanup registration leak
